# WO-626: Block atlas: nightly load-only checks of request pages
Status: queued (after 621)
Vendor: claude
Agent: automation-engineer (Theo Park), devops-engineer (Dana)
Kind: engine
Tier: deep
Severity: HIGH
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Target release: 0.7
Source: owner direction 2026-11-11. Spec: docs/EVIDENCE_ENGINE.md. Reworded after the qa-security review SEC-EE-1 (the first version could have submitted fake identities on opt-out forms).
Boundary: shared rule 5, shared rule 9, LEVERAGE boundary 2 (never submit untrue information), "never fake identities on forms". A block is evidence, never something to work around.

## Task
Each night, on in-house machines only, LOAD each broker's request page (opt-out form, deletion form, privacy page) at most once per surface.
- Never fill a field, submit a form, click, or retry. Just load, read the status, the frame hosts and the vendor headers, and stop.
- Results go into a separate `CanaryObservation` record (broker id, surface, class, vendor, http status, observed time, origin = "datacenter" or "inhouse-residential"). It has no profile and no state, and is never an `ObstructionRecord`.
- A change in a broker's class opens a work order automatically.
- Canary results are routing hints only. They NEVER feed a complaint or the public obstruction index (E3) unless real-user `ObstructionRecord`s from the person's own computer confirm the same class. Blocks seen from datacenter addresses are labelled as such and are not called obstruction anywhere.

## Acceptance
- A test proves the canary code never calls fill/type/click/submit (grep plus runtime spy).
- `CanaryObservation` has no profile or PII field.
- A test shows canary results alone can't produce an ObstructionRecord or an index entry.
- Origin labelling is present.
- Zero personal data in the output.
